Assessment.Summary: The scene effectively establishes the power dynamic between Adrian and Dr. Thorne through concrete sensory details and restrained dialogue. The prose maintains a consistent tone of clinical detachment versus Adrian's vulnerability, with strong causal progression from the intake office to the examination room. The ending lands on a resonant note of transactional relief, fitting the character's desperate situation.

Findings.Explanation: The prose frequently restates the emotional or thematic implication of actions that have already been clearly conveyed through dialogue and physical description. For example, after Thorne's flat delivery of 'Sit' and 'Name,' the narration explicitly states his voice was 'utterly without warmth' and that he viewed Adrian as 'data points.' Similarly, after the physical examination, the text explicitly states Adrian was 'selling his body' and that Thorne's touch was 'devoid of any human warmth.' These explanations dilute the impact of the concrete details by telling the reader what to feel rather than allowing the clinical precision of the actions to speak for themselves.
Findings.RevisionGuidance: Trim the explanatory sentences that interpret the characters' motivations or the nature of the interaction. Trust the concrete details (the flat voice, the mechanical typing, the clinical touch) to convey the power dynamic and Adrian's commodification without explicit thematic labeling.
EvidenceQuotes: "Sit," the man said. His voice was low, precise, and utterly without warmth. It was the voice of someone who had never once in his life needed to ask for anything.
The man typed. The sound of the keys was mechanical, fast, and rhythmic. He did not look up. He did not acknowledge Adrian’s presence except as a series of data points to be entered into a system.
Adrian’s stomach clenched. He watched the doctor’s hands, pale and steady, as they moved over his lower abdomen. The touch was clinical, devoid of any human warmth. It was an inventory. A count.

Thorne moved his hands lower, checking for abnormalities. The touch was impersonal, almost mechanical. Adrian stared at the ceiling, at the water-stained tiles, focusing on the patterns, on the cracks, anything to keep his mind from the invasive reality of what was happening to his body. He was selling it. He was selling his body, inch by inch, for the right to stay in school.
